image_description: A close-up, slightly low-angle shot of a vintage audio cassette tape. The casing is black plastic with a white paper label on the top face featuring red handwritten text and some printed black text. Two circular windows reveal the white spools inside, connected by dark magnetic tape. A rectangular opening at the bottom exposes the tape path. There are visible signs of wear, including scuffs on the label and yellowing/discoloration on the bottom edge.

artifact_observations.reasoning: The red handwritten text on the label is stylized but largely illegible/nonsensical, resembling AI-generated 'fake handwriting' rather than coherent words. Some characters merge or lack proper structure.
The yellow discoloration at the bottom right appears slightly smeared and lacks the crisp texture of aged plastic or sticker residue, suggesting a minor generative blur or texture synthesis issue.
The magnetic tape between the spools looks somewhat indistinct and lacks the sharp, thin line definition expected of real magnetic tape, appearing slightly 'mushy' or fused with the background.

selected_experts.reason: To confirm the object is correctly classified as a cassette and not a similar rectangular object (e.g., VHS, case).
To analyze the legibility and coherence of the handwritten text on the label, checking for AI text artifacts.
To verify the physical continuity of the plastic shell and ensure no floating parts or boundary bleeding between the label and casing.
To assess the realism of the wear patterns (scratches, yellowing) and detect subtle texture inconsistencies.

focus_areas: Legibility and structure of handwritten text on the label
Physical plausibility of the tape path and spool connection
Texture realism of the aged plastic and label paper
Geometric consistency of the rectangular housing and circular windows
custom_prompts_for_reflector: Pay close attention to the handwritten text on the label; AI often struggles with coherent handwriting, producing gibberish that looks plausible at a glance. Also, inspect the magnetic tape itself—it should be a thin, distinct strip, not a blurred blob. Check if the 'wear and tear' (yellowing/scuffs) looks physically applied or digitally smeared.
